samples.summary: Design doc still specifies the pre-clamp `computeTableLayout` snippet and unbounded `rowHeights` semantics
samples.evidence: `docs/design/docs/tables/docs-table-resize.md:200-210` prescribes the exact code this delta replaced (`const userHeight = tableData.rowHeights[r];` — no `normalizeRowHeight`), and lines 41-49 define `rowHeights[i]` as "user-specified minimum height in px" with no numeric band and no mention that a non-finite/non-positive entry now reads as auto. The behaviour contract for `TableData.rowHeights` changed at both CRDT read boundaries and at `computeTableLayout`, so this spec is now the old contract in writing. It lives under `docs/design/docs/tables/`, a NESTED design doc, so the backticked-path lane does not recurse into it and nothing else checks staleness. The site that needs the edit is the doc, not the new code.

samples.summary: The `listLevel` numeric-band section documents both read boundaries; the sibling `rowHeights` band this delta introduces is recorded nowhere
samples.evidence: `docs/design/docs/docs.md:175-188` is the section this PR added to describe the analogous `listLevel` band ("clamps it at both read boundaries (`treeNodeToBlock` and `YorkieDocStore`'s block parser)"). This delta adds a structurally identical invariant — `rowHeights` finite in `(0, MAX_ROW_HEIGHT]`, clamped at `crdt-tree.ts:203`, `yorkie-doc-store.ts:460` and again at `table-layout.ts:253` — and no design doc mentions `MAX_ROW_HEIGHT` at all (grep across `docs/` returns zero hits). A future reader of the table docs has no way to learn that a stored height above 10000 is silently capped or that `0` now means auto.

samples.summary: `Doc.setRowHeight` still persists an unbounded height, so the stored CRDT value can sit above `MAX_ROW_HEIGHT` while every reader shows the clamp
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:1177-1184` writes `td.rowHeights[rowIndex] = height` with no normalization, and its only caller `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2228` computes `Math.max(currentHeight + deltaPx, 20)` — a lower bound only. After this delta the read/layout side caps at 10000, so a stored 12000 renders as 10000: the writer's local model and every peer's normalized model disagree on the persisted number, and a subsequent drag reads the clamped `tl.rowHeights[drag.index]` rather than the value it wrote. Nothing crashes (layout and both read boundaries clamp), so this is drift rather than breakage, but the write path is now the one place in the pipeline that does not know about the band. Fix belongs in `setRowHeight` (call `normalizeRowHeight`), not in the new module.
